class.name: GameplayMessageRouter
class.brief_description: Fire-and-forget message bus keyed by gameplay tag name.
class.description:
For the announcements that have no natural owner: a hit landed, a wave started, the run ended. Wiring those as signals means every listener has to reach the emitter first, and for UI built before the level exists that is a lifetime problem rather than a design one. A channel name is reachable from anywhere and costs nothing to hold. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: GameplayMessageRouter.get_singleton().register_listener(&"Fx.Impact", _on_impact)
func _on_impact(_channel: StringName, payload: Variant) -> void: burst(payload.position, payload.strength) [/codeblock] Channels are tag names, so the hierarchy comes for free: a listener on [code]Fx[/code] registered with [constant MATCH_PARTIAL] hears [code]Fx.Impact[/code] and [code]Fx.Text[/code] alike. Channel names are [b]not[/b] resolved through [GameplayTagsManager] - broadcasting must never register a tag as a side effect - but declaring them in a [GameplayTagTable] anyway documents the channels a project uses and puts them in the tag picker. This is a bus, not a contract. Nothing guarantees anyone is listening, nothing is queued for a listener that registers later, and delivery is synchronous: [method broadcast] returns after the last listener has run. Prefer a signal whenever the emitter and the listener can see each other. The router earns its place when they cannot.

method.name: broadcast
method.description: Calls every matching listener as [code]callback(channel, payload)[/code], in an unspecified order. The channel is passed because a [constant MATCH_PARTIAL] listener cannot otherwise tell what it heard. Listeners are collected before any of them runs, so a listener may broadcast again, register, or unregister itself without disturbing the delivery in progress.

method.name: clear
method.description: Drops every listener. Rarely needed - a listener whose object has been freed is removed on the next broadcast anyway.

method.name: has_listeners
method.description: Whether a [method broadcast] on this channel would reach anyone. Worth checking before building an expensive payload.

method.name: register_listener
method.description: Returns a handle for [method unregister_listener], or [code]0[/code] if the channel is empty or the callable is invalid. A listener whose object is freed is dropped on the next broadcast, so unregistering is good manners rather than a requirement - which is what makes this usable from nodes that come and go with a level.

method.name: unregister_listener
method.description: A no-op for a handle that was never registered or is already gone.

constants.constant: Only messages broadcast on exactly this channel.
This channel and everything below it: a listener on [code]Fx[/code] hears [code]Fx.Impact[/code].
